findings.where: First screen at both widths, and the whole sheet: no place is shown for Mark's photograph
findings.fault: The sheet never shows how a photograph of Mark sits on the blueprint ground. It has no portrait, no captioned placeholder and no photo frame. The only picture is the drawing of the aqueduct. The look leaves out the person, so the next round has no answer for how the man himself appears in this direction.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. Client value 3 ('The man himself: Mark is seen and heard'), which every tile must answer, and first-visit trust item 1 both need a real face. A development-bank officer deciding whether to write to a solo advisor looks for the person, and this tile gives them only a monument.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the section drawing above the name
findings.fault: At 390 px the drawing shrinks to a thin strip about 130 px tall. Mark's name, the role lines, the pitch paragraph and the amber button then fill most of the screen. The direction's one principle is 'the picture leads and the words wait', and on a phone the words lead.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose Threlfall reference and client value 2 ('Calm first: one quiet moving picture before any text asks for anything') are the reason this direction exists. A visitor on a phone, likely arriving from a LinkedIn link, sees a block of text and a button rather than the calm picture.

findings.where: First screen, the name block: the circled 'A' beside MARK M. MOSELEY and the caption 'LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS' under 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR'
findings.fault: Drawing jargon sits in the role line, set in the same spaced capitals as Mark's real role. It looks like part of who he is. The circled 'A' beside the name looks like an initial or a step number. 'NTS' appears three times on the first screen (in the dimension line, the title block and this caption). Directly under his name, a stranger cannot tell the drawing's furniture from facts about Mark.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency officer on a first visit, who reads the role line to learn what Mark does and finds 'Longitudinal section A-A'. Mark also finds busy pages off-putting (§6), and here the decoration crowds into his introduction.

findings.where: Article specimen ('The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'): body text and pull quote over the full blueprint grid
findings.fault: The article page keeps the whole 20 mm and 100 mm grid under its prose. Every line of reading text crosses a lattice of lines. The surface meant for long reading is as busy as the hero sheet.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles (the site's Read mode), who has to read his long, considered argument through the lines. Angélique also cannot change the ground for a long post or a PDF gateway page (client value 9).

findings.where: Type pair tile against the article specimen's title
findings.fault: The type pair says 'Headings in ExtraBold capitals, tracked wide like a drawing title'. The article specimen sets its heading in mixed case and is not tracked. The tile states one heading rule and shows another.
findings.who_objects: The layout round (#8 round 2) and Angélique, who are to draw inside this one look. They get two conflicting heading styles and no rule for which one a post title takes.
